findings.summary: The fixture restoration was not actually unconditional. The explicit restore and the trap-clearing were `;`-separated; the script runs under `set -o pipefail` but without `set -e`, so a failed restore did not stop execution and the next statement disarmed the EXIT trap, stranding the hash-pinned fixture in the mktemp directory with the working tree corrupt in the one file every offset in expected.json depends on.
findings.resolution: The inbound path is now fail-closed. Four guards stand between the test run and `trap - EXIT INT TERM` - the restore mv, an existence re-check of the destination, the re-hash, and the BEFORE/AFTER comparison - each aborting with a non-zero status via an || { echo MARKER >&2; exit 1; } clause rather than falling through. The trap-clearing statement is therefore unreachable except on a proven-restored path, and any failure exits non-zero with the trap still armed, so the EXIT trap fires and retries the restore. The corrected command is written verbatim into the acceptance criterion, a recovery criterion tells the executor to stop rather than re-run when an armed-guard marker appears, and a new must_haves truth and prohibition bind the property.
findings.verification: Not argued - executed. The command shape was run against a stand-in sandbox with a shell function shadowing mv so that only the inbound direction fails. Three modes: (1) restore succeeds -> exit 0, FIXTURE_FAIL_OK printed, fixture present and hash-matching, temp dir removed; (2) restore fails -> exit 1, marker on stderr, and the EXIT trap fires a second restore attempt, proving it was never cleared; (3) abort inside the move/restore window -> exit 9 and the trap restores the file. The previous spelling was run through the same harness for contrast: exit 1, fixture absent from the tree, only copy stranded in the temp dir, and the EXIT trap fired zero times because it had already been cleared.

findings.summary: The escalated "zero skips" acceptance criterion had no corresponding command in the <automated> verify block, which asserted name-set containment and exit status only. Containment covers the 38 baseline skips but would not catch a newly introduced skip, which is what "zero skips" actually asserts.
findings.resolution: Task 2 <automated> now carries an explicit capture-form count: the escalated -json run is captured into a variable, its status taken on the next statement, and two independent conditions asserted - status equals 0, and the count of skip events carrying a "Test" field equals 0. The same spelling is written into the acceptance criteria, with a criterion explaining why it is not redundant with containment. No jq.
findings.verification: Run against stand-ins: zero skips passes; one newly introduced test-level skip fails (the case containment misses); a non-zero test status fails on the separately asserted status. Also confirmed that the inner grep exiting 1 on no matches is harmless in this form, because command substitution yields only the text and the pipeline status never reaches `test` - so the check is safe under pipefail, which was the narrowed ground the orchestrator recorded.

findings.summary: must_haves.truths and the cycle-1 deferral table called the skip/pass comparison "set equality" while the implemented assertion, `comm -23`, is subset containment, and the acceptance criterion already said "set containment". The plan recorded a stronger claim than it tested, and must_haves.truths is what the verifier and summary bind to.
findings.resolution: Relabelled to set containment in both places, with the direction spelled out - the baseline skip set is a subset of the escalated pass set. The check itself is unchanged; containment is the correct property, because the escalated run legitimately passes tests that never skipped. The phrase "set equality" now survives only inside the correction records that describe what was changed.

blocking.summary: The hash-pinned fixture internal/core/domain/segment/testdata/demo.md is moved aside during the unreadable-fixture proof. Restoration is a `trap ... EXIT INT TERM` installed before the move, plus a fail-closed inbound path in which the restore mv, an existence re-check, the re-hash and the BEFORE/AFTER comparison each abort with a non-zero status instead of falling through - so the trap-clearing statement is unreachable except on a proven-restored path, and any failure exits with the trap still armed to retry on EXIT. Both hashes must equal a5f1feb02d617bcc0e2314f8ad6d0df1c7bedd9631f22493c87c57b09917242e. Cycle 2 found the cycle-2 spelling separated the restore from the trap-clearing with a semicolon, which under pipefail without set -e cleared the guard on a failed restore; corrected at cycle 3 and all three control-flow paths executed against a stand-in. Corruption of this one file invalidates all 22 offsets in expected.json and every span assertion in the segment package.

blocking_corrections.reason: The cycle-1 entry recorded as verified ground truth that pgxpool.New 'echoes the connection string verbatim on parse failure', so a malformed DSN carrying a password would reach CI logs. Measured against the pinned pgx/v5 v5.7.2 on four DSN shapes — URL form, keyword/value form, ?password= query, ?sslpassword= query — the library redacts the password on every one, rendering it as `u:xxxxxx` or `password=xxxxx`. A distinctive token placed in the password position produced a grep count of 0 at HEAD against the UNMODIFIED helper. Every canary criterion resting on that premise therefore passed with zero code written: a high-severity, phase-blocking control that could not fail, which is the precise vacuity this milestone exists to remove, reproduced inside the milestone's own plan set.
blocking_corrections.replacement_control: The token moves from the password position to the database-name position, which the library echoes verbatim. Measured at the phase base with the unmodified helper: count 1 on both the URL and keyword/value forms, alongside the library's parse-error text. The criterion now requires 0 for the token, 0 for the parse-error phrasing, a non-zero exit status, and the helper's fixed message present — four independent assertions, and the criterion is measured to FAIL at the phase base, so it can only pass once the branch is rewritten. A unit-level negative control in testenv_test.go first proves the containment assertion can detect the token in a naive rendering before asserting it is absent from the real message.
blocking_corrections.residual_risk: DSN-metadata disclosure (user, host, database name, query parameters) at the pinned version, plus the possibility of a pgx version bump silently dropping the redaction. Both are covered by the same mitigation: the branch emits an argument-free constant, unparseableURLMsg, so no DSN-derived value can reach it without a type change.

blocking_corrections.reason: Same false premise as T-01-01. The standing audit asserted that a password placed in the DSN did not appear in the output; the library already guarantees that, so the audit passed at the phase base with no code written. Rebuilt on the database-name token with positive assertions on exit status and message text, and given its own negative control proving the detector sees the token in a naive rendering.

probe_edges.referent: Simultaneous unsatisfiable conditions. Pool decides in a documented order — unset URL, then unparseable URL, then unreachable host — and names exactly one cause; Fixture runs only after Pool returns, so a fixture condition can never mask a database one. Authored as a truth in 01-01; asserted by 01-03 Scenario B, where both conditions hold at once.

The empty-string flag value returns false from Required; hostFromURL returns the empty string for empty input, a malformed string and a keyword/value DSN, and the unreachable-host branch substitutes a fixed placeholder naming the variable. Authored as a truth in 01-01; pinned by unit tests in Task 1.

Independence from test execution order. Pool and Fixture read the environment on every call and hold no package-level state. Authored as a truth in 01-01; pinned by a -shuffle=on criterion, measured at the phase base to yield the same 38 test-level skips.
